chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever escorts a deceased person until the funeral prayer is performed over him, he will have one 'Qirat' of reward; and whoever accompanies him to his grave until he is buried, he will have two 'Qirats' of reward; and one Qirat is like the mountain of Uhud.

key_terms.جَبَلِ أُحُدٍ: Mount Uhud, used here as a measure of immense reward
key_terms.شَيَّعَ: to escort or accompany (specifically a deceased person)
key_terms.قِيرَاطٌ: a unit of weight/reward, metaphorically large
key_terms.يُصَلِّيَ عَلَيْهِ: the funeral prayer is performed over him

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in reward between escorting a deceased to prayer versus accompanying them to the grave?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes the communal obligation of funeral rites, distinguishing between the reward for escorting the deceased to the prayer (one Qirat) and the greater merit for accompanying them to the grave until burial (two Qirats). The metaphor of a Qirat being equal to Mount Uhud highlights the immense spiritual weight of these acts, reinforcing the Shia tradition of communal solidarity and the social responsibility of the living toward the deceased.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who escorts a deceased until he Prays Salaat over him, there would be for him a ‘Carat’ (reward) from the Recompense; and the one who reaches with him to his grave until he is buried, there would be for him two Carats from the Recompense; and a Carat is like the mountain of Ohad’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from ‘Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If one escorts a deceased until the Salah (prayer) for a deceased is performed, his reward is one qirat and one who escorts the deceased up to the grave and until burial is complete, his reward is two qirat; and one qirat is of the size of the mountain of ‘Uhud.”
